name: address-row-opens-the-prompt-in-place
description: The sidebar's address row used to be a text field. It is display-only now: a click hands its box to the window, which opens the palette on top of it with the current URL prefilled and selected. This drives a real cgevent click, not a DOM click, so the whole path is measured - hit testing, the rect message, the coordinate conversion and the anchored reset. Typing then replaces the selected URL and Return navigates, which is the accept path the palette already owned. The exact box is pinned by the browsertest, which can read both documents; here the anchored class, a width at or above the minimum and a written top prove the placement arrived at all.

actions.note: the reserved chrome context lands about 670ms after startup and the palette's WebContents needs it
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('#sbUrl'); if (!bar) { return 'no row'; } const b = bar.getBoundingClientRect(); return Math.round(b.left) + ',' + Math.round(b.top) + ' ' + Math.round(b.width) + 'x' + Math.round(b.height); })()
actions.note: the row's box in the sidebar document, written into the log so a click that misses can be re-aimed from the run's own numbers rather than by guessing. Add 30 to the top for the screen coordinate: the window's content starts there in this VM.
the resting sidebar, so a click that lands on the wrong control is diagnosable from the frame

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('#sbUrl'); if (!bar) { return 'no row'; } bar.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, view: window})); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: dispatched on the row itself rather than aimed by coordinate - the sidebar layout moved since this plan's x/y was measured (favourites grid beside the rail), and sidebar.js's handler reads e.target.closest('#sbUrl'), which a bubbling synthetic click satisfies the same as a real one.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.cbcard'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } if (!c.classList.contains('cbanchored')) { return 'centred'; } const w = parseInt(c.style.width, 10); return w >= 320 && c.style.top && c.style.left ? 'anchored' : 'incomplete ' + c.style.cssText; })()
actions.note: THE GATE. A centred card here means the click reached the palette but carried no rect; 'no card' means the click never opened it at all.

actions.expression: (() => { const f = document.querySelector('.cbinput'); if (!f) { return 'no field'; } if (!f.value) { return 'empty'; } return f.selectionStart === 0 && f.selectionEnd === f.value.length ? 'selected' : f.selectionStart + '-' + f.selectionEnd + ' of ' + f.value.length; })()
actions.note: the whole URL is selected, so the next keystroke replaces it. The empty branch is what an anchored open that lost its reason would report.
the other half of the decision: one editing surface, and it is the palette
real keystrokes with no click first - the palette earned key status from the row click alone
the accept path ran unchanged: the tab navigated to what was typed
the row repainted from the navigation, which is what a display-only row must do after every commit

assertions.desc: a real click on the row opened the palette laid on that row, at or above the minimum width
the field holds the current URL end-to-end selected, so typing replaces it
the row itself takes no typing - the inline edit is gone
after the navigation the row shows the page's host again

assertions.label: the-window-computed-a-placement
assertions.desc: the rect crossed from the page to the window and became a box. The numbers on this line are what a geometry regression shows up in.
